newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU welcomes new Romanian president with open arms.
newsitem.headline: EU welcomes new Romanian president with open arms.

text.p: The European Commission held out the prospect on Monday of fresh European Union aid to help Romania make urgently needed economic reforms and promised Bucharest's bid to enter the bloc would be taken seriously.

Welcoming new president Emil Constantinescu with open arms -- reflecting a sudden Western outpouring of support for efforts to bring Romania into the Union -- Commission President Jacques Santer said the EU had been encouraged by progress since he took power.

He vowed that despite the political and economic problems Romania has to overcome before joining the bloc, its demand to join the would be considered equally with nine other former communist candidates for membership.
"All countries will be treated equally on merit," he told reporters after meeting Constantinescu.

External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek said that in response to Constantinescu's demand for credits to be unblocked, the EU could release 70 million Ecus ($82 million) in balance of payments aid for Romania once the country had reached an agreement with the International Monetary Fund in loan talks.

The first aim of Constantinescu's visit was to secure financial backing from the EU for a radical free market reform package including a privatisation drive promised by his centrist coalition government.
Van den Broek also said that the Union would favour a new balance of payments assistance programme from the international donor community once Romania's reform process was really working.

"The 70 million Ecus blocked for some time could, after discussions with the IMF, be unblocked by the ministers of the EU," he told reporters. He said he was not sure how long it would take Romania to reach an accord with the IMF.
"I think that the international donor community should then be prepared in case the reform is really being implemented to see whether additional BOP assistance should be given," van den Broek added.
He stressed that for such a new package the donor community, including the G-24, the World Bank and the IMF, would "have to be convinced that the reforms are working."

Constantinescu is in Brussels on his first trip to the west since he triumphed over ex-communists in elections last Novemner to push his country's case for swift membership of both the EU and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO), which he will visit on Tuesday.
Romania already has an association agreement with the EU, but faces a daunting economic challenge before it can become a full member.
